title: 'I don't support the rally': Mamdani opposes RSS chief's Madison Square event

His visit to the United States is part of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's centenary-year global outreach programme. "I don't support the rally, but I don't know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event,” Mamdani said at a news conference on Tuesday.

title: ‘Do we need a 4th-party audit?’ PM raps secretaries over quality of public projects
content: Chairing the monthly Pragati meeting on Tuesday, Modi is learned to have told the top bureaucrats that such things are “unacceptable” and the system won’t work like this. Modi reviewed six infrastructure projects across railway, road and power sectors, spanning nine states with a cumulative cost of over Rs 30,000 crore. He said infrastructure projects should be viewed and monitored as an integrated whole, rather than as isolated sections, stretches or packages.

title: ‘Incredibly emotional’: Anaya Bangar gets CA nod for women’s cricket, eyes WBBL

title: World's first mobile phone call: Cooper dials rival on New York City street
content: Dr Martin Cooper made the first mobile phone call on April 3, 1973.  He called his rival Joel Engel from a New York City street.  Motorola and Bell Laboratories pursued different mobile communication approaches then.  Cooper's call demonstrated a truly portable mobile phone concept.  This event marked an early step in mobile communication evolution.

title: Of 27 lakh ‘logical discrepancy’ deletions in West Bengal, only 7 lakh appealed

title: Congress raises ‘pellet guns’, BJP counters with 1984 riots at panel meet

Chugh’s remarks drew a sharp reaction from Congress MP Jai Prakash, who said the issue was not relevant at all. BJP has accused Congress MP Deepender Hooda of being laudatory in his tribute to Kumar.

title: Dolly Parton passes away at 80: Miley Cyrus, Donald Trump, JK Rowling pay tribute

Many shared their personal experiences and admiration for her spirit.  Her legacy as a songwriter and performer will endure for generations.  The world remembers her kindness, generosity, and immense talent.

title: Zuckerberg’s wife Priscilla Chan’s $125m school to shut after 10 yrs
content: The Primary School, a tuition-free institution for low-income families, has closed its doors after a decade. Funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative ceased, prompting the board's unanimous decision to shut down. While offering extensive support services, the school's academic results did not meet state benchmarks. The Chan Zuckerberg Initiative is providing financial support for the transition and educational savings accounts.

title: Defence minister okays DRDO missile tech transfer to private domestic industry
content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has given the green light for the transfer of missile technology from the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). This strategic decision is set to significantly enhance domestic industries, curtail reliance on imports, and elevate India’s capabilities in defence manufacturing, enabling the local production of guided weapon systems for military applications. Furthermore, this initiative will fortify the defence industrial landscape and encourage the involvement of MSMEs.

title: Minnesota transformed 5,000 acres of old mines into Cuyuna Country
content: A former Minnesota iron mining area has undergone a remarkable ecological transformation over thirty-three years. Abandoned pits and damaged land now host extensive mountain bike trails and natural shorelines. This restoration effort has revitalized nearby communities and created new outdoor tourism opportunities. The clear, deep mine pit lakes also attract scuba divers and anglers from across the region.

title: Residents petition against power plant: Southaven neighbors say xAI site threatens health
content: A family's cherished ancestral land was taken over by a new power plant essential for fueling Elon Musk's artificial intelligence data centers. The relentless din emitted by the facility compelled the family to leave their residence, prompting local residents to voice worries about pollution and degradation in quality of life. They are passionately advocating for cleaner air and a commitment to responsible community development.

title: Cole Tucker, Vanessa Hudgens' combined net worth in 2026: MLB, Hollywood and more

title: Chad Ochocinco hints at Week 3 crossroads for Deshaun Watson's Browns future

Watson will start against Jacksonville, Tampa Bay and potentially Carolina, while Shedeur Sanders remains his backup. Ochocinco pointed to Week 3 as a possible turning point. Watson’s uneven preseason numbers have already added pressure before the regular season begins.

title: Is Darcy Kuemper’s future the Kings’ biggest question before opening night?
content: Darcy Kuemper has a new challenge in Los Angeles Kings training camp, with the starter’s spot no longer a given after a difficult 2025-26 season. Anton Forsberg was a strong presence, starting all four playoff games against the Colorado Avalanche. Kuemper’s play could determine if Los Angeles sticks with its veteran netminder or eventually goes another way with the two goaltenders competing for starts.

title: ‘Separatist’ OCI card holder in SC, seeks nod to visit Kashmir

title: Ram Temple donation ‘scam’ whistleblower gets protection from arrest

title: Revised bullet train cost Rs 2 lakh crore, 2x of original estimate

So far, the funding of Rs 1.1 lakh crore has been from Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and budgetary allocation. They added that Railways has said high-speed trains will be manufactured in India and each of these would cost around Rs 390 crore to Rs 400 crore.

title: 'Her choice': Rahul defends Kriti Sanon after Kangana's barb over Rakhi ad

Sanon further pondered the absurdity of judging cultural values based on attire, affirming that genuine traditions stem from the heart rather than the neck. Earlier, Kangana Ranaut also attacked Sanon's fashion choice and the advertisement's overall styling.

title: NMC pushes old doctors to re-register, but can’t net new ones
content: With over 91,000 MBBS seats available in 2020-21, even with an estimated 75-90% pass percentage, at least 68,000 MBBS graduates should have registered to practice in 2025. Yet the Indian Medical Register shows just over 44,400 entries. That means at least 24,000 of those who graduated just last year are missing from the registry.

title: Dolly Parton, legendary country singer and songwriter, dies at 80
content: Born on January 19, 1946, in Tennessee, Parton grew up in a poor family and was one of 12 children. She began writing songs when she was about six years old. Her first known song, "Little Tiny Tasseltop", was about a corncob doll made with corn-silk hair. Parton was married to Carl Dean from 1966 until his death in 2025. He generally stayed away from the public spotlight.

title: 'Clear Class 10 together': Prashant Kishor's challenge to Bihar CM & Tejashwi
content: Prashant Kishor has thrown down the gauntlet to both Bihar's Chief Minister and opposition leader, challenging them to take their matriculation exams. He proposed that the education minister raise this topic at the upcoming cabinet meeting. This challenge follows the education minister's suggestion for Tejashwi Yadav to pass his exams. Kishor emphasized the need for leaders who inspire trust among the youth by demonstrating their academic capability.

title: Hydel project shutdown triggers power crisis in J&K
content: The prolonged shutdown has widened the region’s power deficit. Jammu & Kashmir’s peak electricity demand stands at about 2,500MW in summer and 3,000MW in winter. With both Baglihar units largely unavailable for most of the past week, Jammu & Kashmir faced a shortfall of nearly 900MW. Built on the Chenab river, Baglihar stages I and II are among Jammu & Kashmir’s key power sources.

title: 8 terror suspects held in Kashmir; arms-ammo, posters seized
content: Six arrests were made in south Kashmir’s Shopian district and two in Pulwama, also in south Kashmir. A cache of arms and ammunition was recovered in north Kashmir’s Sopore district, J&K Police said Tuesday, claiming the action had dealt a major blow to terror networks operating in the Union Territory.

title: 9,000-year-old arrowheads covered in strange markings leave archaeologists puzzled
content: Unearthed from the depths of Turkey, ancient arrowheads reveal enigmatic hand-carved symbols. These Neolithic treasures showcase intentional incisions rather than random scratches, prompting researchers to ponder their origins. Despite thorough investigations, the specific purpose behind these markings remains unknown. Observations indicate that this intriguing practice was limited to select communities, leaving archaeologists grappling with unanswered questions about their significance.

title: AI-powered hackers: The new cyberwar is faster, smarter & harder to stop
content: Artificial intelligence is transforming the landscape of cyber warfare by automating intricate tasks. Recent reports depict AI agents taking charge of substantial segments of cyber operations, drastically cutting down the expertise and duration needed for traditional attack strategies. On the flip side, AI also equips cybersecurity professionals with enhanced capabilities to detect weaknesses. This ongoing battle depicts both sides racing to leverage AI innovations to outsmart each other.

title: Bengaluru clubs under FDA scanner, 10 flagged for violations
content: Food and Drugs Administration officials inspected ten prominent Bengaluru clubs on Tuesday.  Several clubs were found violating food safety and hygiene regulations.  Issues included unhygienic food handling and improper storage practices.  Label violations were also noted on food products found at one club.  These inspections are part of an ongoing drive to ensure compliance.

title: Crude awakening: As Russia, Iran face Trump heat, can Venezuela fill India’s oil gap?
content: What happens when the world stops buying Iran oil due to the threat of secondary sanctions? Where will India procure crude from if it faces tariffs of up to 100% for its Russian crude oil imports? The Middle East crisis has pushed Russia’s share in India’s crude oil basket to over 50%.

title: Asian Games tennis row deepens as AITA rebuts SAI's omission allegation
content: The All India Tennis Association (AITA) has rejected claims it failed to submit the names of excluded Asian Games tennis players to the IOA, with TimesofIndia.com accessing a July 3 letter seeking their inclusion. AITA argued event-specific selections would maximise medal prospects, but the Sports Ministry has stood by its strict Asia-ranking criteria despite criticism from ex-player Rohan Bopanna.

title: Sabalenka, Djokovic knocked out in first round of US Open mixed doubles
content: Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic were knocked out in the first round of the US Open mixed doubles after losing to doubles specialists Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten 1-4, 4-2 (10-2). The top-seeded pair started strongly but failed to maintain their advantage. Patten and Siniakova advanced to the quarterfinals, while other stars including Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz also featured.

title: ‘It was me, not minister Keerthana’: Malaysian woman files plaint over viral video
content: A Malaysian woman, Vinosha Ravi, sought to clear the air after a video went viral, wrongly identifying her as Tamil Nadu minister S Keerthana. Disturbed by the incident, Vinosha reported the matter to Malaysian authorities. She articulated her disappointment over the vicious online discourse and called on the public to stop circulating the video, acknowledging the support she received during this ordeal.

title: 1st in 48 yrs! Sonal Dinusha joins Zaheer Abbas, Everton Weekes in rare feat vs India
content: Sonal Dinusha marked a remarkable achievement in his early Test career against India, scoring three consecutive innings of over 80 runs, a feat shared with cricket legends Everton Weekes and Zaheer Abbas. His determination visibly rattled the Indian bowlers, and his adept use of the sweep shot proved crucial in countering spin. The resilience of the Sri Lankan lower order further thwarted India's attempts to secure victory.

title: Two hours, 500 metres: How Gurgaon’s rain stole my train

Roads remained choked for hours, preventing any significant travel progress.  This recurring infrastructure failure causes financial loss and disrupted plans for residents.  The city's response cycle repeats with every significant downpour.

title: In a first, Rafales take on China's J-16 fighters; why India is watching closely
content: Chinese J-16 fighter jets engaged Egyptian Rafale aircraft in simulated air combat. This exercise provided China rare training against a Western fighter type. The PLA Air Force gained valuable data on Rafale capabilities and tactical behavior. India is closely monitoring this development as it involves a similar fighter. This encounter offers China insights for potential future air engagements.

title: NASA’s $4 billion Roman telescope to map 2 billion galaxies and uncover secrets of the universe
content: This Sunday marks the launch of Nasa's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, a groundbreaking observatory aimed at enhancing our understanding of dark energy and dark matter in the universe. Additionally, it will explore exoplanets beyond our solar system. By conducting expansive wide-field surveys, it will work alongside Hubble and James Webb to map billions of galaxies and cosmic structures, promising exciting advancements in astronomical research.

title: Kansas cowboy turns 50 wind turbines into his most reliable cash crop
content: cattle rancher Pete Ferrell hosts 50 industrial wind turbines on his property . the 150-turbine Elk River Wind Project is a 150-megawatt facility . it generates enough electricity to serve tens of thousands of homes .

title: 3-yr-old’s rape-murder near Bihar border fuels death penalty debate in Nepal
content: the rape and murder of a three-year-old girl in Nepal triggered demands for the death penalty in parliament after days of protests . lawmakers sought constitutional changes to allow capital punishment for heinous crimes . the girl disappeared from jeetpur-Simara on august 16 and her body was recovered two days later from an abandoned house near her home .

title: 2 killed at NHAI construction sites in J&K
content: two workers, aged 25 and 45, died in two separate accidents at NHAI construction sites in samba and jammu districts in J&K on tuesday . a concrete structure collapsed suddenly, killing him on the spot . another worker, also from Bihar, suffered injuries . his wife has been given an immediate relief of Rs 5 lakh from the contractor .

title: ‘Jailed or killed’: How Iran is silencing citizens as internal tensions mount
content: the latest measures come as the country faces mounting economic pressure . sanctions threatening further disruption while the rial has fallen to a record low . a bill titled “Countering the Infiltration of Intelligence Services and Foreign Governments or Institutions in the Country” reportedly makes interviews with foreign media an offence, specifically naming US and Israeli outlets .

title: Israeli military sent US universities millions for weapons research: Report
content: audit records identified more than $15 million in funding linked to the Israeli Ministry of Defense or Israeli defence companies . the investigation found financial links between Israel’s Ministry of defense, weapons manufacturers and dozens of american universities over the past two decades . this included research grants, tuition payments and other forms of institutional funding .
